extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent attorneys, and examiners handling requests for expedited examination at the Korean patent office (KIPO)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for determining eligibility, required evidence, and handling procedures for requests for expedited examination of patent and utility model applications in the Republic of Korea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of expedited examination requested after start of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where expedited examination is requested after the start of examination on an application and the application is eligible for expedited examination, an examiner shall recognize the application to have been requested for expedited examination and conduct expedited examination on the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when an expedited-requested application becomes a prior-filed application claiming domestic priority
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application requested for expedited examination becomes a prior-filed application of an application claiming domestic priority, it is treated differently depending on timing and status: eligibility may be lost, the examiner may order supplementation, dismiss the request, or withhold examination until the prior-filed application is deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key subrules: a prior-filed application is deemed withdrawn when 1 year and 3 months have passed from filing the prior-filed application; if prior-filed status is confirmed before determination the application is not eligible and the examiner orders correction within a designated period and then dismisses if not remedied; if the priority claim is withdrawn before dismissal, the request may be deemed valid; if the application becomes a prior-filed application after determination of expedited eligibility, the examiner shall withhold examination until the application is deemed withdrawn. Also, if a patent is granted on the prior-filed application before withdrawal, a later-filed application cannot be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criterion: application being practiced by a third party (subject)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for an invention or utility model deemed to have been practiced as business by a third party after the laying-open of the application shall be included as a ground for expedited examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'laying-open' of application
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Laying-open of application' refers to the publication of an application specified under Article 64 of the Patent Act; if an application has not been laid open at time of request, the applicant shall request early publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publication is not yet imminent, the requester must file for early publication to meet the requirement; if publication is imminent (e.g., within 15 days), the examiner may defer determination rather than dismissing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'third party' for practicing ground
rubrics_metrics.description: 'A third party' refers to a person other than an applicant and who has not obtained permission to practice the claimed invention or utility model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent particular grounds, the examiner does not need to investigate whether permission exists and may accept the requester's statement as submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'practicing' for ground of third-party practice
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Practicing' refers to acts enumerated under Article 2(3) of the Patent Act / Utility Model Act: for product inventions, manufacturing, using, assigning, leasing, importing, offering for assignment/lease (including display); for method inventions, using the method; for manufacturing-method inventions, acts relating to the product manufactured by the method as well as using the method. Practicing is limited to acts in the Republic of Korea; importation into Korea counts as practicing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of identicalness between third-party practiced invention and claimed invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester must clarify and prove that the invention practiced by a third party is identical with the claimed invention; the requester may submit evidential documents (photos, purchase details, certified mail copies, product samples, etc.) and explanatory descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner compares submitted evidential materials to determine identicalness and may order supplementation if insufficient. If it's difficult for requester to obtain cooperation but identicalness appears highly likely, examiner may accept the request without additional documents except in obvious non-identical cases. If the two inventions are different, the examiner shall dismiss the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible evidential documents for third-party practice claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters can prove third-party practice by submitting documents and descriptions of detailed conditions (time, place, product name, sales numbers), photographs of products, written explanations of purchase time/date and correlation to claimed invention, copies of certified mail (warnings), or other evidential documents or products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples explicitly listed: photographs of product/place, copy of content-certified mail requesting ban on practicing, and other evidential documents or samples; examiner may nevertheless request supplements or accept without additional materials in high-probability scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling request for expedited examination based on practicing prior to laying-open
rubrics_metrics.description: For requests based on third-party practice that occurred before laying-open, the application should be laid open as of the date of determination; if publication is imminent (e.g., within 15 days) or early publication requested, the examiner shall defer determination (not dismiss). Once laid open, expedited examination will be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If early publication request is later dismissed so the application will not be laid open, then the deferred expedited request can be dismissed accordingly; otherwise proceeding occurs upon laying-open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling requests based on applicant's warning to third party
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who received a warning letter about practicing the published invention may request expedited examination by submitting the warning or a copy plus detailed conditions (date, means, contents). The examiner shall recognize the request unless there is a special ground to reject the fact the applicant delivered a warning or the practicing party's product is clearly different from the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject and evidential handling for defense-industry related applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications related to defense industry materials or processes (as defined under relevant Defense Acquisition Program Act provisions) are eligible grounds for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No additional evidential documents are required; a requester may indicate at least one relevant item (e.g., firearms, guided weapons, aircraft, radars, night observation devices, command/control systems) in the written explanation. If the examiner can determine the subject falls under the defense materials list, the request may be recognized without correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green-technology / pollution-prevention applications: subject categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications directly related to green technology and utility model registration applications useful for pollution prevention are eligible for expedited examination and divide into: (1) patent applications on green technology financed or certified by government/etc., and (2) applications on pollution-prevention facilities and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change applies to requests filed since October 1, 2009, and references Article 4(2)(b) and (n) of the Directive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'green technology' for expedited eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Green technology is technology that minimizes greenhouse gas and pollutant emissions and saves/uses energy effectively across socioeconomic activities—examples include greenhouse gas reduction, energy efficiency, cleaner production/energy, resource circulation, eco-friendly technologies, and convergence technologies; it is defined under the Framework Act on Low Carbon Green Growth and Patent Act enforcement decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requester must explain why the claimed invention constitutes green technology in the written explanation; the examiner decides based on the applicant's argument. If there is no ground for denial that the invention saves/uses energy efficiently and minimizes emissions, it shall be recognized as green technology. A non-exhaustive list of major green tech initiatives and '17 new growth engine' technologies is provided as illustrative examples. If no explanation is given or invention appears irrelevant, the examiner shall order correction of the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green-technology applications financed or certified by State: eligible grounds and evidentiary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications may be eligible if the invention is certified as green technology, filed by a certified green business, subsidized by state/local governments, received investment from Green Technology Investment Co., applicant stationed in Green Technology Industrial Cluster, or financed/certified by other national policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners shall verify submission of evidential documents appropriate to each ground (e.g., certification under Article 32, documents linking claimed invention to green business, subsidy evidential documents, investment or loan statements, cluster stationing evidence, R&D financing notices, environmental marks, carbon footprint labels, technology certifications, GR certification, etc.). Applicant and claimed invention must be identical with the person/technology receiving financing/certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications on pollution-prevention facilities and methods: subject and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications whose primary purpose is to prevent/eliminate pollution and which relate to designated environmental pollution prevention facilities or the methods those facilities hold (e.g., noise/vibration control, water pollution preventive facilities, air pollution control equipment, waste disposal facilities, resource-conversion/recycling facilities, sewage/waste treatment plants) are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters need not submit additional evidential documents—merely indicate the facility type in the written explanation. If an application is not related to a facility designated under the relevant environment-related laws, it is not eligible even if it reduces emissions. Examples: an exhaust gas converter installed in a car is not eligible because a car is not a designated air pollutant emitter under the Clean Air Conservation Act. Medical agents or living organisms used directly in operation of such facilities are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications directly related to promotion of export: evidential documents and identicalness
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications directly related to the promotion of export may be eligible if supported by evidential documents such as statement of export result, arrival of letter of credit, buyer's request for patent/utility/design rights, export contracts, evidence of adoption as international standards, or other export-related documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The invention to be exported and the claimed invention must be identical; the requester must prove identicalness. Normally identicalness cannot be determined from request documents alone; however, the examiner can accept the request without requiring additional evidential documents if there is a high possibility they are the same and no particular grounds to doubt it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications related to duties of state or municipal governments: requester identity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications related to duties of state or municipal governments (including duties of national or public schools) are eligible for expedited examination only when the request is made by the state or municipal governments or by an organization exclusively responsible for technology transfer/commercialization set up in national or public schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester is not a qualifying government/organization, the examiner shall order correction within a designated period and dismiss the request if not corrected. Applications filed by an organization exclusively responsible for tech transfer in national/public schools are treated equivalently to state/municipal government requests. National and public schools are defined by governance (state-managed vs municipal-managed); such organizations must be legal entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications of companies certified as venture businesses: evidentiary and timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed by a business confirmed as a venture business under the Act on Special Measures for the Promotion of Venture Businesses is eligible for expedited examination under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination guidelines include: (1) joint filing where one applicant is a venture business — accepted; (2) identical names of venture-certified company and applicant — accepted; (3) at least one of the filing date, date of request for expedited examination, or date of determination must fall within the valid period on the venture certificate; (4) original certificate is preferred to verify status, but a copy may be used if recognized identical; (5) a written notice of evaluation result cannot replace the confirmation certificate.
